title: Time-series and panel data basics

reasoning_review.result: Entity plus calendar-month key defines a lag. Missing dates are not compressed into adjacent periods; December-to-January rollover is correct. The grid distinguishes unreported active operations, nonoperation and observations outside the analysis window. A lag may be observed even when the current value is absent; growth still remains unavailable.

Observed monthly means, endpoint-reported cohorts and complete-window cohorts use different inclusion rules and are correctly distinguished. Complete cases can select future reporting or survival. For the explicit closed-roster sales-flow target only, documented nonoperation contributes zero; an unknown active report prevents a complete total. The continuing/entry/exit identity is an endpoint accounting identity, not a causal effect.

The original one-good model justifies 100 times nominal flow divided by the matched monthly index. Summing those constant-base flows differs from dividing their nominal sum by an unweighted mean index. The chapter distinguishes this construction from official chain aggregation. Flow totals, endpoint stocks, exposure-weighted rates and compounded returns have explicit different targets. Annualized flow levels and annualized growth rates are kept separate.

Weak stationarity is correctly restricted to finite second moments, constant mean and lag-dependent covariance. The MA(1) covariance follows from the shared shock. Counting n-h pairs at lag h derives the exact finite-n average variance. Neither serial dependence nor a stationary dependent law justifies the independent-observation standard error.

reasoning_review.topic: Stationarity versus learning the population mean
reasoning_review.result: The common-component process C+u_t is stationary but its time average converges in mean square to C. The argument establishes averaged-noise mean-square convergence directly, rather than improperly inferring nonconvergence solely from a nonvanishing variance. With nondegenerate C, the probability limit cannot also be the fixed population mean zero.

Deterministic trend changes the mean while the initialized random walk changes variance. Detrending and differencing have the stated different implications; differencing trend-plus-iid noise introduces negative lag-one covariance. The sample ACF convention is explicitly defined, with constant-path and missing-calendar limitations. A short path or zero estimated correlation is not presented as proof of independence or stationarity.

Fixed firm effects and the independence/uncorrelatedness conditions are explicit. Shared variance survives cross-sectional averaging: ten firms do not provide ten independent observations under the stipulated law. Documentation criteria correctly connect inference targets, sampling, time dependence, cross-entity dependence and missingness.
